questions.question: The value of \(\frac{{{{\cos }^4}\theta + {{\sin }^4}\theta + 2{{\sin }^2}\theta {{\cos }^2}\theta }}{{cosec\theta \sec\theta \left( {\sin\theta + \cos\theta - 1} \right)\left( {\sin\theta + \cos\theta + 1} \right)}}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{{{{\cos }^4}\theta + {{\sin }^4}\theta + 2{{\sin }^2}\theta {{\cos }^2}\theta }}{{cosec\theta \sec\theta \left( {\sin\theta + \cos\theta - 1} \right)\left( {\sin\theta + \cos\theta + 1} \right)}}\) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Substitute θ = 45° into the expression as it works for all valid angles.

Numerator = (cos2 45° + sin2 45°)2 = 12 = 1.

Denominator = csc 45° × sec 45° × [(sin 45° + cos 45°)2 − 1].

Denominator = √2 × √2 × [(√2)2 − 1] = 2 × (2 − 1) = 2.

Final Value = Numerator ÷ Denominator = 1/2.

∴ The correct answer is 1/2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression = (cos4θ + sin4θ + 2sin2θ cos2θ) ÷ [cscθ secθ (sinθ + cosθ − 1)(sinθ + cosθ + 1)]

Formula Used:

1. a2 + b2 + 2ab = (a + b)2

2. (a − b)(a + b) = a2 − b2

3. sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

Calculations:

Simplifying the numerator:

⇒ cos4θ + sin4θ + 2sin2θ cos2θ

⇒ (cos2θ + sin2θ)2

⇒ (1)2 = 1

Simplifying the denominator:

⇒ cscθ secθ [(sinθ + cosθ) − 1] [(sinθ + cosθ) + 1]

⇒ (1/sinθ × 1/cosθ) × [(sinθ + cosθ)2 − 12]

⇒ [1 / (sinθ cosθ)] × [sin2θ + cos2θ + 2sinθ cosθ − 1]

⇒ [1 / (sinθ cosθ)] × [1 + 2sinθ cosθ − 1]

⇒ [1 / (sinθ cosθ)] × [2sinθ cosθ]

⇒ 2

Expression value:

⇒ Numerator ÷ Denominator = 1 ÷ 2

∴ The correct answer is 1/2.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

The fundamental identities are sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = csc2θ.

Reciprocal Relations

Trigonometric ratios are related as cscθ = 1/sinθ, secθ = 1/cosθ, and cotθ = 1/tanθ.

Algebraic Expansion in Trig

Expressions like (sinθ + cosθ)2 simplify to 1 + 2sinθcosθ using the identity sin2θ + cos2θ = 1.

questions.question: A certain sum is lent at 4% p.a. for 3 years, 8% p.a. for the next 4 years, and 12% p.a. beyond 7 years. If for a period of 11 years, the simple interest obtained is Rs. 27,600, then the sum is (in Rs):
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum is lent at 4% p.a. for 3 years, 8% p.a. for the next 4 years, and 12% p.a. beyond 7 years. If for a period of 11 years, the simple interest obtained is Rs. 27,600, then the sum is (in Rs):
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Calculate the total effective interest percentage for the entire period.

Total interest % = (4% × 3 years) + (8% × 4 years) + (12% × 4 years)

Total interest % = 12% + 32% + 48% = 92%

Given, 92% of Sum = ₹27,600

⇒ 1% of Sum = 27,600 ÷ 92 = 300

⇒ 100% (Sum) = 300 × 100 = 30,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹30,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Rate 1 (R1) = 4%, Time 1 (T1) = 3 years

Rate 2 (R2) = 8%, Time 2 (T2) = 4 years

Rate 3 (R3) = 12%, Time 3 (T3) = 11 − (3 + 4) = 4 years

Total Simple Interest (SI) = ₹27,600

Formula Used:

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Let the Sum be P.

⇒ Total SI = (P × R1 × T1)/100 + (P × R2 × T2)/100 + (P × R3 × T3)/100

⇒ 27600 = (P × 4 × 3)/100 + (P × 8 × 4)/100 + (P × 12 × 4)/100

⇒ 27600 = (12P + 32P + 48P) ÷ 100

⇒ 27600 = 92P ÷ 100

⇒ P = (27600 × 100) ÷ 92

⇒ P = 300 × 100

⇒ P = 30,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹30,000.

Additional Information

Total Amount in Simple Interest

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI). In percentage terms, A = 100% + (R × T)%.

Effective Interest Rate

When rates vary over different time periods, the net effective rate is the sum of (Ratei × Timei) for each period.

Simple Interest Property

Simple interest is always calculated on the original principal throughout the entire duration of the loan.

questions.question: The areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboidal tank are 3 m 2 , 12 m 2 and 16 m 2 . the capacity of the tank, in litres, is:
questions.questionHtml: The areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboidal tank are 3 m<sup>2</sup>, 12 m<sup>2</sup> and 16 m<sup>2</sup>. the capacity of the tank, in litres, is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of a cuboid (V) = √(Product of areas of three adjacent faces)

V = √(3 × 12 × 16) = √576 = 24 m3

Since 1 m3 = 1000 litres, Capacity = 24 × 1000 = 24000 litres.

∴ The correct answer is 24000 litres.

Alternate Method

Given:

Area of Face 1 (A1) = 3 m2

Area of Face 2 (A2) = 12 m2

Area of Face 3 (A3) = 16 m2

Formula Used:

Volume of Cuboid (V) = length (l) × breadth (b) × height (h)

Adjacent areas: A1 = lb, A2 = bh, A3 = lh

Relationship: V = √(A1 × A2 × A3)

Calculations:

⇒ Let the dimensions of the tank be l, b, and h.

⇒ lb = 3, bh = 12, lh = 16

⇒ (lb) × (bh) × (lh) = 3 × 12 × 16

⇒ l2b2h2 = 576

⇒ (lbh)2 = 576

⇒ lbh = √576 = 24 m3

⇒ Volume of the tank (V) = 24 m3

⇒ We know that 1 m3 = 1000 litres

⇒ Capacity in litres = 24 × 1000 = 24000 litres

∴ The correct answer is 24000 litres.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid

The total surface area (TSA) is given by 2(lb + bh + hl), which is the sum of the areas of all six faces.

Length of Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed in a cuboidal room is the diagonal, calculated as √(l2 + b2 + h2).

Volume of a Cube

For a cube where all sides are equal (l = b = h = a), the volume is V = a3.

Capacity Conversion Units

1 m3 = 1000 litres | 1 litre = 1000 cm3 | 1000 litres = 1 kilolitre (kL).

questions.question: A train of length 287 m, running at 80 km/h, crosses another train moving in the opposite direction at 37 km/h in 18 seconds. What is the length of the other train?
questions.questionHtml: A train of length 287 m, running at 80 km/h, crosses another train moving in the opposite direction at 37 km/h in 18 seconds. What is the length of the other train?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative Speed in opposite direction = 80 + 37 = 117 km/h

Relative Speed in m/s = 117 × 5/18 = 32.5 m/s

Total distance (sum of lengths) = Relative Speed × Time = 32.5 × 18 = 585 m

Length of the other train = 585 − 287 = 298 m

∴ The correct answer is 298 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of first train (L1) = 287 m

Speed of first train (S1) = 80 km/h

Speed of second train (S2) = 37 km/h

Time taken (t) = 18 s

Formula: (L1 + L2) = (S1 + S2) × Time

⇒ Relative speed = (80 + 37) km/h = 117 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 117 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 6.5 × 5 = 32.5 m/s

⇒ Total distance = L1 + L2 = 287 + L2

⇒ 287 + L2 = 32.5 × 18

⇒ 287 + L2 = 585

⇒ L2 = 585 − 287

⇒ L2 = 298 m

∴ The correct answer is 298 m.

Additional Information

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Srel = S1 + S2.

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Srel = |S1 − S2|.

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Total Crossing Distance

When a train crosses another train or a bridge, the total distance covered is the sum of the lengths of both objects (L1 + L2).

questions.question: Study the given graph and answer the question that follows. The number of employees = 3000 The total number of employees working in departments A and C exceeds the total number of employees working in departments B and D by x. The value of x lies between:
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given graph and answer the question that follows.

The number of employees = 3000

The total number of employees working in departments A and C exceeds the total number of employees working in departments B and D by x. The value of x lies between:
questions.solution:
Given:

Total number of employees = 3000

Formula Used:

Number of employees in a department = (x/360°) × Total number of employees

where, x → Angle for employees in department

Calculations:

Total number of employees = 3000

Employees in department A = 64.2° 

⇒ Employees in department A = (64.2°/360°) × 3000 = 535

Employees in department C = 72° 

⇒ Employees in department C = (72°/360°) × 3000 = 600

Total Employees in department A and C = 535 + 600 = 1135      ----(1) 

Employees in department B = 73.8° 

⇒ Employees in department B = (73.8°/360°) × 3000 = 615

Employees in department D = 57° 

⇒ Employees in department D = (57°/360°) × 3000 = 475

Total Employees in department B and D = 615 + 475 = 1090      ----(2) 

Required difference = 1135 – 1090 = 45

⇒ x lies between 44 and 52

Alternate Method

Total angle corresponding to people working in A and C together = 64.2° + 72° = 136.2° 

Total angle corresponding to people working in B and D together = 73.8° + 57° = 130.8° 

Difference between (A + C) and (B + D) = 136.2° - 130.8° = 5.4° Converting the angle to number = 5.4/360 × 3000 = 45

∴ The value of x lies between 44 and 52.

questions.question: Study the given and answer the question that follows. The number of employees = 3000 If 20% of the employees working in department E are transferred to department A, then the difference between the number of employees in A and 124% of the employes working in department C is:
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given and answer the question that follows.

The number of employees = 3000

If 20% of the employees working in department E are transferred to department A, then the difference between the number of employees in A and 124% of the employes working in department C is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Total number of employees = 3000

Formula Used:

If P and Q have x and y things and z things are transferred from P to Q, then

Number of things in P = x – z

Number of things in Q = y + z

Calculations:

Total number of employees = 3000

Employees in department E = 93° 

⇒ Employees in department E = (93°/360°) × 3000 = 775

20% of Employees of department E = (20/100) × 775

⇒ 20% of Employees of department E = 155

Employees in department A = 64.2° 

⇒ Employees in department A = (64.2°/360°) × 3000 = 535

Now, 20% of the employees working in department E are transferred to department A

⇒ Employees in department A = 535 + 155 = 690      ----(1)

Employees in department C = 72° 

⇒ Employees in department E = (72°/360°) × 3000 = 600

124% of Employees in department C = (124/100) × 600 = 744      ----(2)

Required difference = (2) – (1)

⇒ Required difference = 744 – 690 = 54

∴ The difference between the number of employees in A and 124% of the employees working in department C is 54.

questions.question: If \( \frac{5}{4{\sqrt 2 }} + \frac{{3 + 2\sqrt 2 }}{{3 - 2\sqrt 2 }} - \frac{{3 - 2\sqrt 2 }}{{3 + 2\sqrt 2 }} = a + b\sqrt 2 \) , then what is the value of (3a + 4b)?
questions.questionHtml: If \( \frac{5}{4{\sqrt 2 }} + \frac{{3 + 2\sqrt 2 }}{{3 - 2\sqrt 2 }} - \frac{{3 - 2\sqrt 2 }}{{3 + 2\sqrt 2 }} = a + b\sqrt 2 \), then what is the value of (3a + 4b)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using identity: [(x + y)/(x − y)] − [(x − y)/(x + y)] = 4xy / (x2 − y2)

Middle terms = [4 × 3 × 2√2] / [32 − (2√2)2] = 24√2 / (9 − 8) = 24√2

Expression = 5/(4√2) + 24√2 = 5√2/8 + 24√2 = (197/8)√2

Comparing with a + b√2 → a = 0, b = 197/8

Value of (3a + 4b) = 3(0) + 4(197/8) = 197/2 = 98½

∴ The correct answer is 98½.

Alternate Method

Given:

5/(4√2) + (3 + 2√2)/(3 − 2√2) − (3 − 2√2)/(3 + 2√2) = a + b√2

Formula Used:

Rationalization and Algebraic Identity: (x + y)2 − (x − y)2 = 4xy

Calculations:

⇒ Rationalizing first term: 5 / (4√2) = (5 × √2) / (4√2 × √2) = 5√2 / 8

⇒ Simplifying fractions: [(3 + 2√2)2 − (3 − 2√2)2] / [(3 − 2√2)(3 + 2√2)]

⇒ Applying identity: [4 × 3 × 2√2] / [32 − (2√2)2]

⇒ [24√2] / [9 − 8] = 24√2

⇒ Total LHS = (5/8)√2 + 24√2 = (5/8 + 24)√2 = (197/8)√2

⇒ a + b√2 = 0 + (197/8)√2

⇒ On comparison: a = 0 and b = 197/8

⇒ Required value = 3a + 4b = 3(0) + 4(197/8)

⇒ 0 + 197/2 = 98.5 or 98½

∴ The correct answer is 98½.

Additional Information

Rationalization of Surds

To rationalize a denominator of the form (x − y), multiply both numerator and denominator by its conjugate (x + y) so that (x − y)(x + y) = x2 − y2.

Standard Algebraic Identities

(a + b)2 − (a − b)2 = 4ab and (a + b)2 + (a − b)2 = 2(a2 + b2). These are frequently used to simplify symmetric surd fractions.

Comparing Coefficients

When an equation is in the form x + y√k = a + b√k, then x = a and y = b, provided x, y, a, b are rational and √k is irrational.

⇒ Profit of company in 2015 = Rs. 60 cr

Percentage Revenue of company in 2015 = 60/210 × 100 = 28.57%      ----(2)

Profit of company in 2016 = Rs.(200 – 175) cr

⇒ Profit of company in 2016 = Rs. 25 cr

Percentage Revenue of company in 2016 = 25/200 × 100 = 12.5%      ----(3)

Profit of company in 2017 = Rs.(240 – 200) cr

⇒ Profit of company in 2017 = Rs. 40 cr

⇒ Profit of company in 2018 = Rs. 55 cr

questions.question: A and B are solutions of acid and water. The ratios of water and acid in A and B are 4 : 5 and 1 : 2 respectively. If x liters of A is mixed with y liters of B, then the ratio of water and acid in the mixture becomes 8 : 13 What is x : y?
questions.questionHtml: A and B are solutions of acid and water. The ratios of water and acid in A and B are 4 : 5 and 1 : 2 respectively. If x liters of A is mixed with y liters of B, then the ratio of water and acid in the mixture becomes 8 : 13 What is x : y?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Water fraction in A = 4/9 and in B = 1/3.

Water fraction in the resultant mixture = 8/21.

Using Alligation: x : y = (8/21 − 1/3) : (4/9 − 8/21).

x : y = (1/21) : (4/63) ⇒ 3/63 : 4/63 = 3 : 4.

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of water and acid in A = 4 : 5

Ratio of water and acid in B = 1 : 2

Final ratio in mixture = 8 : 13

Formula Used:

Alligation Rule: (Quantity of A / Quantity of B) = (Fraction in B − Mean Fraction) / (Mean Fraction − Fraction in A)

Calculations:

⇒ Fraction of water in solution A = 4 / (4 + 5) = 4/9

⇒ Fraction of water in solution B = 1 / (1 + 2) = 1/3

⇒ Fraction of water in the final mixture = 8 / (8 + 13) = 8/21

⇒ x / y = (8/21 − 1/3) ÷ (4/9 − 8/21)

⇒ x / y = [(8 − 7) / 21] ÷ [(28 − 24) / 63]

⇒ x / y = (1/21) ÷ (4/63)

⇒ x / y = (1/21) × (63/4)

⇒ x / y = 3 / 4

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4.

Additional Information

Alligation Rule

It is used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices/concentrations must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired price/concentration.

Component Consistency

When applying alligation, ensure all values represent the same component (either all acid fractions or all water fractions).

Mean Value Property

The mean value (mixture concentration) must always lie between the individual concentrations of the two components being mixed.

questions.question: The numerator of fraction is 3 more than the denominator. When 5 is added to the numerator and 2 is subtracted from the denominator, the fraction becomes 8/3, When the original fraction is divided by \(5 \frac{1}{2}\) , the fraction so obtained is:
questions.questionHtml: The numerator of fraction is 3 more than the denominator. When 5 is added to the numerator and 2 is subtracted from the denominator, the fraction becomes 8/3, When the original fraction is divided by \(5 \frac{1}{2}\), the fraction so obtained is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume Denominator = x, then Numerator = x + 3.

Condition: (x + 3 + 5) ÷ (x − 2) = 8/3 ⇒ (x + 8) / (x − 2) = 8/3.

By cross-multiplication: 3x + 24 = 8x − 16 ⇒ 5x = 40 ⇒ x = 8.

Original Fraction = (8 + 3) / 8 = 11/8.

New Fraction = (11/8) ÷ (11/2) = (11/8) × (2/11) = 1/4.

∴ The correct answer is 1/4.

Alternate Method

Given:

Numerator (N) = Denominator (D) + 3

Divisor = 5 1/2 = 11/2

Formula used: Division of fractions (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = (a/b) × (d/c)

⇒ Let the denominator be d.

⇒ Numerator = d + 3.

⇒ According to the question: (d + 3 + 5) / (d − 2) = 8/3

⇒ (d + 8) / (d − 2) = 8/3

⇒ 3 × (d + 8) = 8 × (d − 2)

⇒ 3d + 24 = 8d − 16

⇒ 8d − 3d = 24 + 16

⇒ 5d = 40

⇒ d = 8

⇒ Original fraction = (d + 3) / d = 11/8

⇒ Mixed fraction 5 1/2 = 11/2

⇒ Result = (11/8) ÷ (11/2) = (11/8) × (2/11)

⇒ Result = 2/8 = 1/4

∴ The correct answer is 1/4.

Additional Information

Proper and Improper Fractions

A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than the denominator (e.g., 1/4), while an improper fraction has a numerator equal to or greater than the denominator (e.g., 11/8).

Division of Fractions

To divide one fraction by another, multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction: (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = (a/b) × (d/c).

Mixed Numbers to Improper Fractions

To convert a mixed number x a/b, use the formula: (x × b + a) / b. For example, 5 1/2 = (5 × 2 + 1) / 2 = 11/2.

questions.question: In ΔABC, the bisector of ∠A intersects side BC at D. If AB = 12 cm, AC = 15 cm and BC = 18 cm, then the length of BD is
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, the bisector of ∠A intersects side BC at D. If AB = 12 cm, AC = 15 cm and BC = 18 cm, then the length of BD is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By Angle Bisector Theorem, the bisector of an angle divides the opposite side in the ratio of the other two sides.

Ratio of BD : DC = AB : AC = 12 : 15 = 4 : 5.

Total units = 4 + 5 = 9 units.

Given total length BC = 18 cm.

BD = (4 ÷ 9) × 18 = 8 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Triangle ABC where AB = 12 cm, AC = 15 cm, and BC = 18 cm.

AD is the internal bisector of ∠A meeting BC at D.

Formula Used:

Internal Angle Bisector Theorem: In ΔABC, if AD is the bisector of ∠A, then AB / AC = BD / DC.

Calculations:

⇒ BD / DC = AB / AC

⇒ BD / DC = 12 / 15

⇒ BD / DC = 4 / 5

⇒ Let BD = 4x and DC = 5x

⇒ BC = BD + DC = 4x + 5x = 9x

⇒ 18 = 9x

⇒ x = 18 ÷ 9 = 2

⇒ BD = 4x = 4 × 2 = 8 cm

∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.

Additional Information

Internal Angle Bisector Theorem

The internal bisector of an angle of a triangle divides the opposite side internally in the ratio of the sides containing the angle: BD/DC = AB/AC.

External Angle Bisector Theorem

The external bisector of an angle of a triangle divides the opposite side externally in the ratio of the sides containing the angle: BE/CE = AB/AC.

Length of the Angle Bisector

The length of the internal bisector AD can be calculated using the formula: AD2 = AB × AC − BD × DC.

Incenter Property

The three internal angle bisectors of a triangle are concurrent at a point called the incenter, which is equidistant from all sides of the triangle.

questions.question: The lengths of two sides of a parallelogram are 3 cm and 10 cm. What is the sum of the squares of the diagonals of the parallelogram?
questions.questionHtml: The lengths of two sides of a parallelogram are 3 cm and 10 cm. What is the sum of the squares of the diagonals of the parallelogram?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of squares of diagonals = 2 × (Sum of squares of adjacent sides)

Adjacent sides are 3 cm and 10 cm.

Sum = 2 × (32 + 102)

Sum = 2 × (9 + 100) = 2 × 109 = 218 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 218 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given: Sides of parallelogram a = 10 cm and b = 3 cm.

Formula Used: d12 + d22 = 2(a2 + b2), where d1 and d2 are the diagonals.

⇒ Let the two diagonals be d1 and d2.

⇒ Using the property: d12 + d22 = 2(side12 + side22)

⇒ d12 + d22 = 2(102 + 32)

⇒ d12 + d22 = 2(100 + 9)

⇒ d12 + d22 = 2 × 109

⇒ d12 + d22 = 218 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 218 cm2.

Additional Information

Area of Parallelogram

The area of a parallelogram is given by Base × Height or a × b × sin(θ), where θ is the angle between adjacent sides.

Diagonal Properties

The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. They divide the parallelogram into two congruent triangles and four triangles of equal area.

Rhombus Special Case

For a rhombus, where all sides (a) are equal, the formula becomes d12 + d22 = 4a2, and the diagonals bisect each other at 90°.

questions.question: The monthly incomes of A and B are in the ration 3 : 5 and the ratio of their savings is 2 : 3 If the income of B is equal to three times the savings of A, then what is the ratio of the expenditures of A and B?
questions.questionHtml: The monthly incomes of A and B are in the ration 3 : 5 and the ratio of their savings is 2 : 3 If the income of B is equal to three times the savings of A, then what is the ratio of the expenditures of A and B?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Income ratio A : B = 3 : 5 and Savings ratio A : B = 2 : 3.

Condition: Income of B = 3 × Savings of A.

To align units, make Income of B (5 parts) equal to 3 × Savings of A (2 parts) ⇒ 5x = 6y ⇒ x/y = 6/5.

New Income A : B = (3×6) : (5×6) = 18 : 30.

New Savings A : B = (2×5) : (3×5) = 10 : 15.

Expenditure ratio = (18−10) : (30−15) = 8 : 15.

∴ The correct answer is 8 : 15.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of monthly incomes (A : B) = 3 : 5

Ratio of savings (A : B) = 2 : 3

Condition: Income of B = 3 × Savings of A

Formula Used:

Expenditure = Income − Savings

Calculations:

⇒ Let Income of A = 3x and Income of B = 5x

⇒ Let Savings of A = 2y and Savings of B = 3y

⇒ According to the condition: 5x = 3 × 2y

⇒ 5x = 6y

⇒ x/y = 6/5

⇒ Let x = 6 and y = 5

⇒ Income of A = 3 × 6 = 18 units

⇒ Income of B = 5 × 6 = 30 units

⇒ Savings of A = 2 × 5 = 10 units

⇒ Savings of B = 3 × 5 = 15 units

⇒ Expenditure of A = 18 − 10 = 8 units

⇒ Expenditure of B = 30 − 15 = 15 units

⇒ Ratio of Expenditures = 8 : 15

∴ The correct answer is 8 : 15.

Additional Information

Income-Expenditure Fundamental

The basic accounting identity used in such problems is Income = Expenditure + Savings.

Ratio Balancing Technique

To compare two different ratios, we must find a common link (multiplier) based on the given constraint to bring them to the same unit scale.

Percentage Change in Expenditure

If income increases by a% and savings increase by b%, the new expenditure can be found using the same linear relationship: Inew − Snew = Enew.

questions.question: X and Y enter into a partnership with capital in the ratio 3 ∶ 5 After 5 months X adds 50% of his capital, while Y withdraws 60% of his capital. What is the share (in Rs. lakhs) of X in the annual profit of Rs. 6.84 lakhs?
questions.questionHtml: X and Y enter into a partnership with capital in the ratio 3 ∶ 5 After 5 months X adds 50% of his capital, while Y withdraws 60% of his capital. What is the share (in Rs. lakhs) of X in the annual profit of Rs. 6.84 lakhs?
questions.solution:
Let X's and Y's initial investment for the first 5 months be 30 and 50

After 5 months,

X's capital for next 7 months = (150/100) × 30 = 45

Y's capital for next 7 months = (40/100) × 50 = 20

(X's profit)/(Y's profit) = [(30 × 5) + (45 × 7)]/[(50 × 5) + (20 × 7)]

⇒ (150 + 315)/(250 + 140) ⇒ 465/390 ⇒ 31/26

Total profit = 31 + 26 = 57 units

⇒ (X's profit)/(Total profit) = 31/57

⇒ (X's profit)/6.84 = 31/57 ⇒ X's profit = 3.72

questions.question: The average of three numbers a, b and c is 12 more than c. The average of a and b is 48. If d is 10 less than c, then the average of c and d is:
questions.questionHtml: The average of three numbers a, b and c is 12 more than c. The average of a and b is 48. If d is 10 less than c, then the average of c and d is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Average of a and b = 48 → Sum (a + b) = 96.

Average of a, b, c = c + 12 → (96 + c) ÷ 3 = c + 12.

96 + c = 3c + 36 ⇒ 2c = 60 ⇒ c = 30.

Given d = c − 10 ⇒ d = 30 − 10 = 20.

Average of c and d = (30 + 20) ÷ 2 = 25.

∴ The correct answer is 25.

Alternate Method

Given:

Average of a, b, c = c + 12

Average of a, b = 48

d = c − 10

Formula Used:

Average = (Sum of values) ÷ (Number of values)

Calculations:

⇒ (a + b) ÷ 2 = 48

⇒ a + b = 48 × 2 = 96

⇒ (a + b + c) ÷ 3 = c + 12

⇒ 96 + c = 3(c + 12)

⇒ 96 + c = 3c + 36

⇒ 3c − c = 96 − 36

⇒ 2c = 60 ⇒ c = 30

⇒ d = c − 10 = 30 − 10 = 20

⇒ Average (c, d) = (30 + 20) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 50 ÷ 2 = 25

∴ The correct answer is 25.

Additional Information

Arithmetic Average Properties

If every number in a set is increased or decreased by a constant k, the average also increases or decreases by k.

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups with averages A1 and A2 and sizes n1 and n2 are combined, the new average is (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For a series in Arithmetic Progression (AP), the average is simply (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

questions.question: The radius and height of a right circular cone are in the ratio 3 : 4. If its curved surface area (in cm 2 ) is 240 π, then its volume (in cm 3 ) is:
questions.questionHtml: The radius and height of a right circular cone are in the ratio 3 : 4. If its curved surface area (in cm<sup>2</sup>) is 240 π, then its volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of r : h : l = 3 : 4 : 5 (standard Pythagorean triplet).

Let r = 3x, h = 4x, and slant height l = 5x.

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = πrl = π × (3x) × (5x) = 15πx2.

Given CSA = 240π ⇒ 15πx2 = 240π ⇒ x2 = 16 ⇒ x = 4.

Volume = (1/3) × π × (3x)2 × (4x) = 12πx3 = 12π × (4)3 = 12π × 64 = 768π cm3.

∴ The correct answer is 768π cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of radius (r) and height (h) = 3 : 4

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 240π cm2

Formula Used:

Slant height (l) = √(r2 + h2)

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = πrl

Volume of Cone (V) = (1/3) × π × r2 × h

Let radius r = 3x and height h = 4x.

⇒ l = √((3x)2 + (4x)2) = √(9x2 + 16x2) = √(25x2) = 5x cm

⇒ CSA = π × r × l = π × 3x × 5x = 15πx2

⇒ 15πx2 = 240π

⇒ x2 = 240 ÷ 15 = 16

⇒ x = √16 = 4

⇒ Radius (r) = 3 × 4 = 12 cm

⇒ Height (h) = 4 × 4 = 16 cm

⇒ Volume (V) = (1/3) × π × (12)2 × 16

⇒ Volume (V) = (1/3) × π × 144 × 16

⇒ Volume (V) = 48 × 16 × π = 768π cm3

∴ The correct answer is 768π cm3.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The TSA of a cone is the sum of its curved area and base area: TSA = πrl + πr2 = πr(l + r).

Pythagorean Relation in Cone

In any right circular cone, the height, radius, and slant height always satisfy l2 = h2 + r2.

Volume Comparison

The volume of a cone is exactly 1/3 the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height: Vcone = (1/3)Vcylinder.

Frustum Volume

For a frustum of a cone with radii R and r and height h: Volume = (1/3)πh(R2 + r2 + Rr).

questions.question: Anuja owns \(66 \frac{2}{3}\%\) of a property. If 30% of the property that she owns is worth Rs. 1,25,000, then 45% of the value (in Rs) of the property is:
questions.questionHtml: Anuja owns \(66 \frac{2}{3}\%\) of a property. If 30% of the property that she owns is worth Rs. 1,25,000, then 45% of the value (in Rs) of the property is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Anuja share = 66 2/3% = 2/3 of total property.

Given 30% of her share = 30% × 2/3 = 1/5 of total property.

1/5 unit = ₹1,25,000.

Total Property (1 unit) = ₹1,25,000 × 5 = ₹6,25,000.

Required 45% of property = 45% of 6,25,000 = ₹2,81,250.

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,81,250.

Alternate Method

Given:

Anuja ownership = 66 2/3% of the total property.

30% of Anuja ownership = ₹1,25,000.

Formula Used:

Value = Total × Ownership Fraction × Part Fraction

Calculations:

⇒ Let the total value of the property be V.

⇒ Anuja share = 66 2/3% of V = (200/3)% × V = 2/3 × V.

⇒ 30% of Anuja share = 30/100 × (2/3 × V) = 1,25,000.

⇒ (3/10) × (2/3) × V = 1,25,000.

⇒ (1/5) × V = 1,25,000.

⇒ V = 1,25,000 × 5 = ₹6,25,000.

⇒ Required value = 45% of V = (45/100) × 6,25,000.

⇒ Required value = 45 × 6,250 = ₹2,81,250.

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,81,250.

Additional Information

Percentage to Fraction conversion

Common fractions include 33 1/3% = 1/3, 66 2/3% = 2/3, and 20% = 1/5. Using fractions simplifies multiplication in multi-step percentage problems.

Successive Percentage formula

When calculating a percentage of a percentage, the net percentage is (x/100) × (y/100) × 100. For example, 30% of 66 2/3% results in exactly 20% of the base value.

Unitary Method in Percentage

If a specific percentage 'p' of a quantity equals 'x', then 100% of the quantity equals (x ÷ p) × 100.

questions.question: The sum of radii spheres A and B is 14 cm, the radius of A being larger than that of B. The difference between their surface areas is 112 π. What is the ratio of the volumes of A and B?
questions.questionHtml: The sum of radii spheres A and B is 14 cm, the radius of A being larger than that of B. The difference between their surface areas is 112 π. What is the ratio of the volumes of A and B?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of radii (RA + RB) = 14 cm

Difference in Surface Areas: 4π(RA2 − RB2) = 112π

RA2 − RB2 = 28 ⇒ (RA + RB)(RA − RB) = 28

14 × (RA − RB) = 28 ⇒ RA − RB = 2 cm

Solving RA+RB=14 and RA−RB=2 gives RA = 8 cm and RB = 6 cm

Ratio of Radii = 8 : 6 = 4 : 3 ⇒ Volume Ratio = 43 : 33 = 64 : 27

∴ The correct answer is 64 : 27.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of Sphere A = RA, Radius of Sphere B = RB (RA > RB)

Sum: RA + RB = 14 cm

Surface Area of Sphere = 4πr2

Volume of Sphere = (4/3)πr3

According to the question:

⇒ 4πRA2 − 4πRB2 = 112π

⇒ 4π(RA2 − RB2) = 112π

⇒ RA2 − RB2 = 112 / 4 = 28

⇒ (RA + RB)(RA − RB) = 28

⇒ 14 × (RA − RB) = 28

⇒ RA − RB = 2

Adding the two equations:

⇒ (RA + RB) + (RA − RB) = 14 + 2

⇒ 2RA = 16 ⇒ RA = 8 cm

⇒ RB = 14 − 8 = 6 cm

Ratio of Volumes = [(4/3)πRA3] / [(4/3)πRB3]

⇒ Volume Ratio = (RA / RB)3

⇒ Volume Ratio = (8 / 6)3 = (4 / 3)3

⇒ Volume Ratio = 64 / 27

∴ The correct answer is 64 : 27.

Additional Information

Properties of Spheres

The surface area (S) of a sphere is 4πr2 and the volume (V) is (4/3)πr3.

Ratios of Similar 3D Figures

If the ratio of the radii of two spheres is a : b, then the ratio of their surface areas is a2 : b2 and the ratio of their volumes is a3 : b3.

Algebraic Identities in Geometry

The identity a2 − b2 = (a + b)(a − b) is frequently used to solve difference in area problems when the sum or difference of dimensions is known.

questions.question: The perimeters of ΔABC and ΔDEF are 43.2 cm and 28.8 cm, respectively, and ΔABC ~ ΔDEF. If DE = 12 cm, then the length of AB is:
questions.questionHtml: The perimeters of ΔABC and ΔDEF are 43.2 cm and 28.8 cm, respectively, and ΔABC ~ ΔDEF. If DE = 12 cm, then the length of AB is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For similar triangles, the ratio of perimeters is equal to the ratio of corresponding sides.

Perimeter(ΔABC) ÷ Perimeter(ΔDEF) = AB ÷ DE

43.2 ÷ 28.8 = AB ÷ 12

1.5 = AB ÷ 12

AB = 1.5 × 12 = 18 cm

∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Perimeter of ΔABC (P1) = 43.2 cm

Perimeter of ΔDEF (P2) = 28.8 cm

Length of side DE = 12 cm

ΔABC ~ ΔDEF

Formula Used:

If ΔABC ~ ΔDEF, then AB ÷ DE = BC ÷ EF = AC ÷ DF = Perimeter(ΔABC) ÷ Perimeter(ΔDEF)

Calculations:

⇒ AB ÷ DE = Perimeter(ΔABC) ÷ Perimeter(ΔDEF)

⇒ AB ÷ 12 = 43.2 ÷ 28.8

⇒ AB ÷ 12 = 432 ÷ 288

⇒ AB ÷ 12 = 3 ÷ 2 (Dividing both by 144)

⇒ AB = (3 × 12) ÷ 2

⇒ AB = 36 ÷ 2

⇒ AB = 18 cm

∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.

Additional Information

Area Ratio Property

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(Δ1) ÷ Area(Δ2) = (Side1 ÷ Side2)2.

Altitude and Median Ratio

For similar triangles, the ratio of their corresponding altitudes, medians, and angle bisectors is also equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides and perimeters.

AA Similarity Criterion

Two triangles are similar if two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of the other triangle (Angle-Angle similarity).

questions.question: If 27(x + y) 3 - 8(x - y) 3 = (x + 5y)(Ax 2 + By 2 + Cxy), then what is the value of (A + B - C)?
questions.questionHtml: If 27(x + y)<sup>3</sup> - 8(x - y)<sup>3</sup> = (x + 5y)(Ax<sup>2</sup> + By<sup>2</sup> + Cxy), then what is the value of (A + B - C)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply the value substitution method by letting x = 1 and y = −1.

LHS = 27(1 − 1)3 − 8(1 − (−1))3 = 27(0) − 8(2)3 = −64.

RHS = (1 + 5(−1))(A(1)2 + B(−1)2 + C(1)(−1)) = −4(A + B − C).

Equating LHS and RHS: −64 = −4(A + B − C) ⇒ A + B − C = 16.

∴ The correct answer is 16.

Alternate Method

Given: 27(x + y)3 − 8(x − y)3 = (x + 5y)(Ax2 + By2 + Cxy)

Formula used: a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + b2 + ab)

⇒ Let a = 3(x + y) and b = 2(x − y).

⇒ (a − b) = 3(x + y) − 2(x − y) = 3x + 3y − 2x + 2y = x + 5y.

⇒ a2 = [3(x + y)]2 = 9(x2 + y2 + 2xy) = 9x2 + 9y2 + 18xy.

⇒ b2 = [2(x − y)]2 = 4(x2 + y2 − 2xy) = 4x2 + 4y2 − 8xy.

⇒ ab = 3(x + y) × 2(x − y) = 6(x2 − y2) = 6x2 − 6y2.

⇒ (a2 + b2 + ab) = (9x2 + 4x2 + 6x2) + (9y2 + 4y2 − 6y2) + (18xy − 8xy) = 19x2 + 7y2 + 10xy.

⇒ Comparing coefficients with Ax2 + By2 + Cxy: A = 19, B = 7, C = 10.

⇒ A + B − C = 19 + 7 − 10 = 16.

∴ The correct answer is 16.

Additional Information

Sum and Difference of Cubes

The fundamental identities are a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) and a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2).

Algebraic Expansion

The cube of a binomial is (a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3a2b + 3ab2 and (a − b)3 = a3 − b3 − 3a2b + 3ab2.

Identity Matching

When an identity holds for all values of x and y, you can substitute arbitrary values (like x = 1, y = 0 or y = −1) to find the values of unknown constants A, B, and C quickly.

questions.question: When 1062, 1134 and 1182 are divided by the greatest numbers x, remainder in each case is y. What is the value of (x - y)?
questions.questionHtml: When 1062, 1134 and 1182 are divided by the greatest numbers x, remainder in each case is y. What is the value of (x - y)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When numbers leave the same remainder, the divisor x is the HCF of their differences.

Differences: (1134 − 1062) = 72 and (1182 − 1134) = 48.

x = HCF(72, 48) = 24.

y = Remainder when 1062 ÷ 24 = 6.

Value of (x − y) = 24 − 6 = 18.

∴ The correct answer is 18.

Alternate Method

Given: Numbers are 1062, 1134, and 1182. Divisor is x and common remainder is y.

Formula Used: If n1, n2, n3 leave the same remainder y when divided by x, then x = HCF(|n1 − n2|, |n2 − n3|, |n3 − n1|).

⇒ First difference = 1134 − 1062 = 72

⇒ Second difference = 1182 − 1134 = 48

⇒ Third difference = 1182 − 1062 = 120

⇒ x = HCF(72, 48, 120)

⇒ 72 = 24 × 3, 48 = 24 × 2, 120 = 24 × 5

⇒ x = 24

⇒ To find y, divide 1062 by 24: 1062 = (24 × 44) + 6

⇒ y = 6

⇒ Required value = x − y = 24 − 6 = 18

∴ The correct answer is 18.

Additional Information

HCF and Same Remainder Property

The largest number that divides several numbers leaving the same remainder is the HCF of the absolute differences between those numbers.

Case of Known Remainder

If the remainder R is given, then the greatest divisor is HCF of (Number1 − R), (Number2 − R), and (Number3 − R).

Euclidean Algorithm

HCF(a, b) = HCF(b, a mod b). This is the fastest way to calculate the HCF of two large numbers manually.

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 43.2 minutes and 108 minutes, respectively. Pipe C can empty it at 3 litres/minute. When all the three pipes are opened together, they fill the tank in 54 minutes. The capacity (in litres) of the tank is:
questions.questionHtml: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 43.2 minutes and 108 minutes, respectively. Pipe C can empty it at 3 litres/minute. When all the three pipes are opened together, they fill the tank in 54 minutes. The capacity (in litres) of the tank is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Convert times to a common base: Pipe A = 43.2 = 216/5 min, Pipe B = 108 min, All = 54 min.

Take LCM of (216/5, 108, 54) = 216 units as total capacity.

Efficiencies: A = 5, B = 2, (A+B−C) = 4 units/min.

Efficiency of Pipe C = (Eff A + Eff B) − (Combined Eff) = (5 + 2) − 4 = 3 units/min.

Since Efficiency of C is 3 litres/min, then 3 units = 3 litres ⇒ 1 unit = 1 litre.

∴ The correct answer is 216 litres.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by Pipe A = 43.2 minutes = 216/5 minutes

Time taken by Pipe B = 108 minutes

Time taken by (A + B − C) = 54 minutes

Rate of Pipe C = 3 litres/minute

Formula Used:

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Capacity = Total Work units × (Actual rate ÷ Calculated efficiency)

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
Pipe A 216/5 min 216 units 5
Pipe B 108 min 2
A + B − C 54 min 4

Calculations:

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe C = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − Efficiency of (A + B − C)

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe C = 5 + 2 − 4

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe C = 3 units/minute

⇒ According to the question, efficiency of C = 3 litres/minute

⇒ 3 units = 3 litres

⇒ 1 unit = 1 litre

⇒ Total capacity of the tank = 216 units = 216 × 1 litre

⇒ Total capacity = 216 litres

∴ The correct answer is 216 litres.

Additional Information

Pipes and Cisterns Basic Rule

If a pipe fills a tank in X hours and another empties it in Y hours, the net work done in 1 hour is (1/X − 1/Y). A positive result means the tank is filling.

Capacity Calculation

Capacity of tank = (Emptying rate in L/min) × (Time taken by the emptying pipe alone to empty the full tank).

LCM Method for Fractions

LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators. This is used when time is given in decimals or fractions like 43.2 = 216/5.

questions.question: Given that x 8 - 34x 4 + 1 = 0, x > 0. What is the value of (x 3 + x -3 )?
questions.questionHtml: Given that x<sup>8</sup> - 34x<sup>4</sup> + 1 = 0, x > 0. What is the value of (x<sup>3</sup> + x<sup>-3</sup>)?
questions.solution:
Calculations :

x8 - 34x4 + 1 = 0 

Divide both the sides of the equation by x4 , then equation will become 

x4 - 34 + x-4 = 0 

⇒ x4 + x-4 = 34 

Adding 2 to both the sides of the equation 

x4 + x-4 + 2 = 36 

⇒ (x2 + x-2)2 = 36 

⇒ x2 + x-2 = 6 

Again adding 2 to both the sides of the equation 

x2 + x-2 + 2 = 8 

⇒ (x1 + x-1)2  = 8 

⇒ x + x-1 = 2√2 

Now cube both the sides of the equation 

(x + x-1)3 = (2√2)3 

⇒ x3 + x-3 = 10√2 

∴ The value of x3 + x-3 = 10√2

questions.question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 15 cm is melted and recast into spherical balls of radius 3 cm each. What is the ratio of the surface area of original sphere and sum of the surface areas of all the balls?
questions.questionHtml: A solid metallic sphere of radius 15 cm is melted and recast into spherical balls of radius 3 cm each. What is the ratio of the surface area of original sphere and sum of the surface areas of all the balls?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of original Surface Area to the sum of Surface Areas of n small balls is given by r : R.

Here, R = Radius of large sphere = 15 cm.

r = Radius of small balls = 3 cm.

Ratio = 3 : 15 = 1 : 5.

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of large sphere (R) = 15 cm

Radius of small ball (r) = 3 cm

Formula:

Volume of Sphere = (4/3)πr3

Surface Area of Sphere = 4πr2

Calculations:

⇒ Number of small balls (n) = (Volume of large sphere) ÷ (Volume of one small ball)

⇒ n = [(4/3) × π × 153] ÷ [(4/3) × π × 33]

⇒ n = 153 ÷ 33 = (15/3)3 = 53 = 125 balls

⇒ Surface Area of original sphere (SA1) = 4 × π × 152 = 4 × π × 225 = 900π cm2

⇒ Total Surface Area of all small balls (SA2) = 125 × (4 × π × 32)

⇒ SA2 = 125 × 4 × π × 9 = 4500π cm2

⇒ Required Ratio = SA1 : SA2 = 900π : 4500π

⇒ Ratio = 900 : 4500 = 1 : 5

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 5.

Additional Information

Melting and Recasting

When a solid is melted and recast into another shape, the total volume remains constant (Volumeinitial = Volumefinal).

Scaling of Properties

If the linear dimensions are changed by a factor k, the surface area changes by k2 and the volume changes by k3.

Total Surface Area vs Single Surface Area

While volume is conserved during recasting, the total surface area always increases when a larger object is broken into multiple smaller objects.

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{{0.0203 \times 2.92}}{{0.7 \times 0.0365 \times 2.9}} \div \frac{{{{\left( {12.12} \right)}^2} - {{\left( {8.12} \right)}^2}}}{{{{\left( {0.25} \right)}^2} + \left( {0.25} \right)\left( {19.99} \right)}}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{{0.0203 \times 2.92}}{{0.7 \times 0.0365 \times 2.9}} \div \frac{{{{\left( {12.12} \right)}^2} - {{\left( {8.12} \right)}^2}}}{{{{\left( {0.25} \right)}^2} + \left( {0.25} \right)\left( {19.99} \right)}}\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{0.0203 \times 2.92}{0.7 \times 0.0365 \times 2.9} \div \frac{(12.12)^2 - (8.12)^2}{(0.25)^2 + (0.25)(19.99)}\)

Formula used:

a2 - b2 = (a + b)(a - b)

Calculation:

\(\frac{0.0203 \times 2.92}{0.7 \times 0.0365 \times 2.9} \div \frac{(12.12)^2 - (8.12)^2}{(0.25)^2 + (0.25)(19.99)}\)

⇒ \(\frac{203 \times 292 \times 10^{-6}}{7 \times 365 \times 29 \times 10^{-6}} \div \frac{(12.12 + 8.12)(12.12 - 8.12)}{0.25(0.25 + 19.99)}\)

⇒ \(\frac{29 \times 292}{365 \times 29} \div \frac{20.24 \times 4}{0.25 \times 20.24}\)

⇒ \(\frac{4}{5} \div \frac{4}{0.25}\)

⇒ \(0.8 \div 16\)

⇒ 0.05

∴ The correct answer is option (1).

questions.question: cosA(secA - cosA)(cotA + tanA)=?
questions.questionHtml: cosA(secA - cosA)(cotA + tanA)=?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Put A = 45° in the expression.

cos 45° = 1/√2, sec 45° = √2, cot 45° = 1, tan 45° = 1.

Expression = (1/√2) × (√2 − 1/√2) × (1 + 1).

Expression = (1/√2) × (1/√2) × 2 = (1/2) × 2 = 1.

From the options, tan 45° = 1.

∴ The correct answer is tan A.

Alternate Method

Given: cos A (sec A − cos A) (cot A + tan A)

Formula Used: sec A = 1/cos A; cot A = cos A/sin A; tan A = sin A/cos A; sin2 A + cos2 A = 1.

⇒ cos A (1/cos A − cos A) (cos A/sin A + sin A/cos A)

⇒ (cos A × 1/cos A − cos2 A) ((cos2 A + sin2 A) / (sin A cos A))

⇒ (1 − cos2 A) (1 / (sin A cos A))

⇒ sin2 A × (1 / (sin A cos A))

⇒ (sin A × sin A) / (sin A × cos A)

⇒ sin A / cos A

⇒ tan A

∴ The correct answer is tan A.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental identities include sin2 A + cos2 A = 1, 1 + tan2 A = sec2 A, and 1 + cot2 A = cosec2 A.

Reciprocal Relations

Trigonometric ratios are related as sec A = 1/cos A, cosec A = 1/sin A, and cot A = 1/tan A.

Combined Ratio Identity

The sum of tan A and cot A always simplifies to 1 / (sin A × cos A) or sec A × cosec A.

questions.question: Directions: Study the given graph and answer the question that follows. The number of employees = 3000 The number of employees in department B is what percent of the total number of employees working in department D and E?
questions.questionHtml:

∴ The required percentage is 49.3%

questions.question: If the 5-digit number 535ab is divisible by 3, 7 and 11 then what is the value of (a 2 - b 2 + ab)?
questions.questionHtml: If the 5-digit number 535ab is divisible by 3, 7 and 11 then what is the value of (a<sup>2</sup> - b<sup>2</sup> + ab)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

LCM of 3, 7, and 11 is 231.

Dividing 53500 by 231 gives a remainder of 139.

The number is 53500 + (231 − 139) = 53592.

Comparing 53592 with 535ab gives a = 9 and b = 2.

Value = 92 − 22 + (9 × 2) = 81 − 4 + 18 = 95.

∴ The correct answer is 95.

Alternate Method

Given that the 5-digit number 535ab is divisible by 3, 7, and 11.

LCM of 3, 7, 11 = 3 × 7 × 11 = 231.

⇒ Assume the maximum possible value for the number is 53599.

⇒ 53599 ÷ 231 ⇒ Quotient = 232, Remainder = 7.

⇒ Correct multiple = 53599 − 7 = 53592.

⇒ Comparing 53592 with 535ab ⇒ a = 9, b = 2.

⇒ Required expression: (a2 − b2 + ab)

⇒ Value = 92 − 22 + (9 × 2)

⇒ Value = 81 − 4 + 18 = 95.

∴ The correct answer is 95.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 3, 7, and 11

A number is divisible by 3, 7, and 11 if it is divisible by their LCM, which is 231. This is because 3, 7, and 11 are prime numbers.

Divisibility Rule of 11

The difference between the sum of digits at odd places and even places must be 0 or a multiple of 11. For 53592: (5 + 5 + 2) − (3 + 9) = 12 − 12 = 0.

LCM of Prime Numbers

For any set of prime numbers, the Least Common Multiple (LCM) is the product of those numbers: LCM(p1, p2, p3) = p1 × p2 × p3.

questions.question: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is increased by 20% and the height is decreased by 30%, then what is the percentage increase/decrease in the volume?
questions.questionHtml: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is increased by 20% and the height is decreased by 30%, then what is the percentage increase/decrease in the volume?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of cylinder is proportional to r2h.

Net multiplier = (1 + 20/100)2 × (1 − 30/100)

Net multiplier = (1.2)2 × 0.7 = 1.44 × 0.7 = 1.008

Change = (1.008 − 1) × 100 = 0.8% increase.

∴ The correct answer is Increase 0.8%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius increase = 20%

Height decrease = 30%

Formula Used:

Volume of Right Circular Cylinder (V) = πr2h

Calculations:

⇒ Let original radius = r and original height = h

⇒ Original Volume (V1) = πr2h

⇒ New radius (r′) = r + 20% of r = 1.2r

⇒ New height (h′) = h − 30% of h = 0.7h

⇒ New Volume (V2) = π(1.2r)2(0.7h)

⇒ V2 = π(1.44r2)(0.7h) = 1.008 πr2h

⇒ Change in volume = V2 − V1 = 1.008πr2h − πr2h = 0.008πr2h

⇒ % Change = (0.008πr2h ÷ πr2h) × 100 = 0.8%

∴ The correct answer is Increase 0.8%.

Additional Information

Cylinder Properties

Volume = πr2h | Curved Surface Area = 2πrh | Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h).

Successive Percentage for 3D Figures

If dimensions change by a%, b%, and c%, then net volume change multiplier is (1 + a/100)(1 + b/100)(1 + c/100).

Comparison with Sphere/Cone

Sphere volume V = (4/3)πr3 (depends on r3). Cone volume V = (1/3)πr2h (same factor dependency as cylinder).

questions.question: The area (in sq. units) of the triangle formed by the graphs of 8x + 3y = 24, 2x + 8 = y and the x-axis is:
questions.questionHtml: The area (in sq. units) of the triangle formed by the graphs of 8x + 3y = 24, 2x + 8 = y and the x-axis is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Intersection with x-axis (set y = 0):

Line 1 (8x + 3y = 24) → 8x = 24 → x = 3. Point: (3, 0)

Line 2 (2x + 8 = y) → 2x = −8 → x = −4. Point: (−4, 0)

Base on x-axis = 3 − (−4) = 7 units.

Intersection of both lines (Height): 8x + 3(2x + 8) = 24 ⇒ 14x = 0 ⇒ x = 0, y = 8. Height = 8 units.

Area = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 7 × 8 = 28.

∴ The correct answer is 28 sq. units.

Alternate Method

Given:

Line 1: 8x + 3y = 24

Line 2: 2x − y = −8

Line 3: y = 0 (x-axis)

Formula Used:

Area of Triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height

Calculations:

To find the vertices of the triangle:

Vertex A: Intersection of 8x + 3y = 24 and y = 0.

⇒ 8x + 3(0) = 24 ⇒ 8x = 24 ⇒ x = 3. Point A = (3, 0).

Vertex B: Intersection of 2x + 8 = y and y = 0.

⇒ 2x + 8 = 0 ⇒ 2x = −8 ⇒ x = −4. Point B = (−4, 0).

Vertex C: Intersection of 8x + 3y = 24 and 2x − y = −8.

From second line, y = 2x + 8. Substitute in first line:

⇒ 8x + 3(2x + 8) = 24

⇒ 8x + 6x + 24 = 24

⇒ 14x = 0 ⇒ x = 0.

⇒ y = 2(0) + 8 = 8. Point C = (0, 8).

Base of triangle (on x-axis) = xA − xB = 3 − (−4) = 7 units.

Height of triangle = y-coordinate of vertex C = 8 units.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × Base × Height

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 7 × 8 = 28 sq. units.

∴ The correct answer is 28 sq. units.

Additional Information

Area using Coordinates

For vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2), and (x3, y3), Area = 1/2 |x1(y2−y3) + x2(y3−y1) + x3(y1−y2)|.

Intercept Form

A line ax + by = c can be written as x/(c/a) + y/(c/b) = 1, where c/a is the x-intercept and c/b is the y-intercept.

Intersection with Axes

To find the x-intercept, set y = 0. To find the y-intercept, set x = 0 in the linear equation.

questions.question: A is 80% more than B and C is 48(4/7) % less than the sum of A and B. By what per cent is C less than A?
questions.questionHtml: A is 80% more than B and C is 48(4/7) % less than the sum of A and B. By what per cent is C less than A?
questions.solution:
Given:

A = B + 80% of B

C = (A + B) - 48\(\frac{4}{7}\)% of (A + B)

Formula used:

Percentage less = \(\frac{Difference}{Base} \times 100\)

Calculation:

Let B = 100

⇒ A = 100 + 80 = 180

⇒ A + B = 180 + 100 = 280

⇒ 48\(\frac{4}{7}\)% = \(\frac{340}{7} \% = \frac{340}{700} = \frac{17}{35}\)

⇒ C = 280 × \((1 - \frac{17}{35})\)

⇒ C = 280 × \(\frac{18}{35}\)

⇒ C = 8 × 18 = 144

⇒ Difference between A and C = 180 - 144 = 36

⇒ Percentage less = \(\frac{36}{180} \times 100\)

⇒ \(\frac{1}{5} \times 100\) = 20%

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: In a school 3/8 of the number of students are girls and the rest are boys. One-third of the number of boys are below 10 years and 2/3 the number of girls are also below 10 years. If the number of students of age 10 or more years is 260. then the number of boys in the school is:
questions.questionHtml: In a school 3/8 of the number of students are girls and the rest are boys. One-third of the number of boys are below 10 years and 2/3 the number of girls are also below 10 years. If the number of students of age 10 or more years is 260. then the number of boys in the school is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Total Students = 24 units (LCM of 8 and 3).

Girls = 3/8 × 24 = 9 units; Boys = 15 units.

Boys 10+ years = 15 × (1 − 1/3) = 15 × 2/3 = 10 units.

Girls 10+ years = 9 × (1 − 2/3) = 9 × 1/3 = 3 units.

Total 10+ years = 10 + 3 = 13 units → 260 students.

1 unit = 20 ∴ Boys = 15 × 20 = 300.

∴ The correct answer is 300.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of Girls = 3/8 of total students

Ratio of Boys = 5/8 of total students

Boys below 10 years = 1/3 of boys

Girls below 10 years = 2/3 of girls

Students 10 years or more = 260

Formula used:

Part = Total × Fraction

⇒ Let total students be x.

⇒ Number of Girls = (3/8)x

⇒ Number of Boys = (5/8)x

⇒ Boys 10 years or older = (1 − 1/3) × (5/8)x = (2/3) × (5/8)x = (10/24)x

⇒ Girls 10 years or older = (1 − 2/3) × (3/8)x = (1/3) × (3/8)x = (3/24)x

⇒ Total students (10+ years) = (10/24)x + (3/24)x = (13/24)x

⇒ (13/24)x = 260

⇒ x = (260 × 24) ÷ 13

⇒ x = 20 × 24 = 480

⇒ Number of Boys = (5/8) × 480 = 5 × 60 = 300

∴ The correct answer is 300.

Additional Information

Fractional Breakdown

If a group is divided into parts A and B, and a sub-fraction f of A is selected, the absolute value is Total × (Ratio of A) × f.

Unitary Method for Ratios

When fractions have different denominators (8 and 3), assuming the total as their LCM (24) simplifies calculations by avoiding decimals.

Complementary Fractions

If a fraction p is below a threshold, the remaining part is always (1 − p). This is useful for finding "10 years or older" when "below 10 years" is given.

questions.question: A certain number of students from school X appeared in an examination and 30% of the students failed. 150% more students than those from school X, appeared in the same examination from school Y. If 80% of the total number of students who appeared from X and Y passed, then what is the percentage of students who failed from Y?
questions.questionHtml: A certain number of students from school X appeared in an examination and 30% of the students failed. 150% more students than those from school X, appeared in the same examination from school Y. If 80% of the total number of students who appeared from X and Y passed, then what is the percentage of students who failed from Y?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of students in School X : School Y = 100 : (100 + 150) = 100 : 250 = 2 : 5.

Total Fail% = 100% − 80% = 20%.

Using Weighted Average: (RatioX × Fail%X + RatioY × Fail%Y) ÷ Total Ratio = Total Fail%.

(2 × 30 + 5 × Fail%Y) ÷ 7 = 20 ⇒ 60 + 5 × Fail%Y = 140.

5 × Fail%Y = 80 ⇒ Fail%Y = 16%.

∴ The correct answer is 16%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Fail % in School X = 30%

Students in School Y = 150% more than School X

Total Pass % (X + Y) = 80%

Calculations:

⇒ Let the number of students from School X = 100

⇒ Students from School Y = 100 + 150% of 100 = 100 + 150 = 250

⇒ Total students (X + Y) = 100 + 250 = 350

⇒ Total Pass rate = 80% ⇒ Total Fail rate = 100% − 80% = 20%

⇒ Total number of failed students = 20% of 350 = 70

⇒ Failed students from School X = 30% of 100 = 30

⇒ Failed students from School Y = Total failed − Failed from X = 70 − 30 = 40

⇒ Percentage of failed students from Y = (Failed from Y ÷ Total from Y) × 100

⇒ Fail % in Y = (40 ÷ 250) × 100 = 16%

∴ The correct answer is 16%.

Additional Information

Percentage Change and "More Than" Concept

If a value B is x% more than A, then B = A × (1 + x/100). If B is x% of A, then B = A × (x/100).

Weighted Average Formula

The combined average of two groups with sizes n1, n2 and averages a1, a2 is given by (n1a1 + n2a2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Alligation Rule

Ratio of quantities = (Higher Value − Mean Value) : (Mean Value − Lower Value). This is useful for finding individual group percentages.

questions.question: The radii of two right circular cylinders are in the ratio 3 : 2 and the of their volumes is 27 : 16. What is the ratio of their heights?
questions.questionHtml: The radii of two right circular cylinders are in the ratio 3 : 2 and the of their volumes is 27 : 16. What is the ratio of their heights?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of a cylinder (V) ∝ r2 × h

⇒ Height (h) ∝ V ÷ r2

Ratio of heights (h1 : h2) = (V1 ÷ r12) : (V2 ÷ r22)

⇒ h1 : h2 = (27 ÷ 32) : (16 ÷ 22) = (27 ÷ 9) : (16 ÷ 4) = 3 : 4

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of radii (r1 : r2) = 3 : 2

Ratio of volumes (V1 : V2) = 27 : 16

Formula Used:

Volume of cylinder (V) = πr2h

Calculations:

⇒ Let radii be 3x and 2x, and heights be h1 and h2.

⇒ V1 / V2 = (π × r12 × h1) / (π × r22 × h2)

⇒ 27 / 16 = (32 × h1) / (22 × h2)

⇒ 27 / 16 = (9 × h1) / (4 × h2)

⇒ h1 / h2 = (27 × 4) / (16 × 9)

⇒ h1 / h2 = (3 × 1) / (4 × 1)

⇒ h1 : h2 = 3 : 4

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4.

Additional Information

Surface Area of Cylinder

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh and Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(h + r).

Volume Ratios for Solid Figures

For a cone, V = (1/3)πr2h. The ratio of volumes depends on both r2 and h, similar to the cylinder.

Relationship between Dimensions

If height is constant, V1/V2 = (r1/r2)2. If radius is constant, V1/V2 = h1/h2.

questions.question: An article is marked 35% above its cost. If a profit of 20% is earned by selling the article, then the discount per cent offered on the marked price of the article is:
questions.questionHtml: An article is marked 35% above its cost. If a profit of 20% is earned by selling the article, then the discount per cent offered on the marked price of the article is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100.

Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 35 = 135.

Selling Price (SP) = 100 + 20 = 120 (since Profit = 20%).

Discount = MP − SP = 135 − 120 = 15.

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (15 ÷ 135) × 100 = 100/9 % = 11 1/9 %.

∴ The correct answer is 11 1/9 %.

Alternate Method

Given:

Markup Percentage = 35%

Profit Percentage = 20%

Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit/100)

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup/100)

Discount % = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be ₹100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 35% of 100 = 100 + 35 = ₹135.

⇒ Profit = 20% on Cost Price.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100 + 20% of 100 = 100 + 20 = ₹120.

⇒ Discount offered on Marked Price = MP − SP

⇒ Discount = 135 − 120 = ₹15.

⇒ Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (15 ÷ 135) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 9) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 100/9 % = 11 1/9 %.

∴ The correct answer is 11 1/9 %.

Additional Information

The CP-MP Relationship

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be expressed as: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit %) ÷ (100 − Discount %).

Effective Profit Formula

Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − [(Markup % × Discount %) ÷ 100]. This is derived from the successive percentage change formula.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), whereas Profit or Loss is generally calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

questions.question: How many kg of rice costing Rs. 42 per kg should be mixed with \(7\frac{1}{2}\) kg rice costing Rs. 50 per kg so that by selling the mixture at Rs. 53.10 per kg, there is gain of 18%?
questions.questionHtml: How many kg of rice costing Rs. 42 per kg should be mixed with \(7\frac{1}{2}\) kg rice costing Rs. 50 per kg so that by selling the mixture at Rs. 53.10 per kg, there is gain of 18%?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Step 1: Calculate the Mean Cost Price (CP) of the mixture = 53.10 ÷ 1.18 = ₹45/kg.

Step 2: Use Alligation ratio of Rice1 (₹42) and Rice2 (₹50) with Mean (₹45).

Step 3: Ratio = (50 − 45) : (45 − 42) = 5 : 3.

Step 4: 3 units represent 7.5 kg (given), so 1 unit = 2.5 kg.

Step 5: Quantity of first rice = 5 units = 5 × 2.5 = 12.5 kg.

∴ The correct answer is 12½ kg.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of Rice1 (CP1) = ₹42/kg

Cost of Rice2 (CP2) = ₹50/kg

Quantity of Rice2 (Q2) = 7.5 kg = 15/2 kg

Selling Price of mixture (SPm) = ₹53.10/kg

Profit percentage = 18%

Formula Used:

Cost Price (CP) = [Selling Price (SP) × 100] ÷ [100 + Profit%]

Rule of Alligation: Q1/Q2 = (CP2 − Mean CP) ÷ (Mean CP − CP1)

Calculations:

⇒ CP of mixture = (53.10 × 100) ÷ (100 + 18)

⇒ CP of mixture = 5310 ÷ 118 = ₹45/kg

⇒ Ratio of Rice1 to Rice2 = (50 − 45) : (45 − 42)

⇒ Q1 : Q2 = 5 : 3

⇒ Given Q2 = 7.5 kg

⇒ 3 units = 7.5 kg

⇒ 1 unit = 7.5 ÷ 3 = 2.5 kg

⇒ Q1 = 5 × 2.5 kg = 12.5 kg

∴ The correct answer is 12½ kg.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It is a rule that enables us to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at the given price must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired price. Ratio = (Dearer Price − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − Cheaper Price).

Cost Price Calculation

When profit is made, CP = SP × [100 / (100 + Profit%)]. Alligation should always be performed on the Cost Price, never directly on the Selling Price unless the profit/loss is zero.

Weighted Average Method

Alternatively, the mean price can be calculated as Pm = (n1p1 + n2p2) / (n1 + n2), where n is the quantity and p is the price per unit.

questions.question: A, B and C started a business. Twice the investment of A is equal to thrice the investment of B and also five times the investment of C. If the total profit after a year is Rs. 15.5 lakhs, then the share of B in the profit is (in Rs. lakhs):
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C started a business. Twice the investment of A is equal to thrice the investment of B and also five times the investment of C. If the total profit after a year is Rs. 15.5 lakhs, then the share of B in the profit is (in Rs. lakhs):
questions.solution:
2A = 3B = 5C, L.C.M of 2, 3 and 5 = 30

So, A = 30/2 = 15, ⇒ B = 30/3 = 10, ⇒ C = 30/5 = 6

Total profit = 15 + 10 + 6 = 31, Share of B = (10/31) × 15.5 lakhs ⇒ Rs. 5 lakhs

questions.question: In a circle with center O, BC is a chord. Points P and A are on the circle, on the opposite side of BC, such that ∠ PBC = 28° and BP = PC. What is the measure of the inverse angle of BOC?
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with center O, BC is a chord. Points P and A are on the circle, on the opposite side of BC, such that ∠ PBC = 28°  and BP = PC. What is the measure of the inverse angle of BOC?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In isosceles ▵PBC, ∠BPC = 180° − (2 × ∠PBC) = 180° − (2 × 28°) = 124°.

Since P is on the minor arc and A is on the major arc, ∠BAC = 180° − ∠BPC = 180° − 124° = 56°.

Central angle ∠BOC = 2 × ∠BAC = 2 × 56° = 112°.

∴ The correct answer is 112°.

Alternate Method

Given: ∠PBC = 28°, BP = PC, O is the center, P and A are on opposite sides of chord BC.

⇒ In ▵PBC, since BP = PC, ∠PCB = ∠PBC = 28°.

⇒ Sum of angles in ▵PBC = 180°

⇒ ∠BPC = 180° − (28° + 28°) = 180° − 56° = 124°.

⇒ Since points A, B, P, C lie on the circle and A, P are on opposite sides of BC, BAPC is a cyclic quadrilateral.

⇒ ∠BAC + ∠BPC = 180° (Opposite angles of a cyclic quad)

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° − 124° = 56°.

⇒ By the central angle theorem, angle at center = 2 × angle at circumference.

⇒ ∠BOC = 2 × ∠BAC = 2 × 56° = 112°.

∴ The correct answer is 112°.

Additional Information

Inscribed Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle (∠Center = 2 × ∠Circumference).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

A quadrilateral is cyclic if all its vertices lie on a circle. The sum of its opposite angles is always 180°.

Angles in an Isosceles Triangle

In a triangle, if two sides are equal, the angles opposite to those sides are also equal.

questions.question: A can do 20% of a work in 4 days. B can do 33.33% work in 10 days. They worked together for 9 days. C complete the remaining work in 6 days. B and C together will complete 75% of the same work in:
questions.questionHtml: A can do 20% of a work in 4 days. B can do 33.33% work in 10 days. They worked together for 9 days. C complete the remaining work in 6 days. B and C together will complete 75% of the same work in:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total time for A = 4 ÷ 20% = 20 days; B = 10 ÷ 33.33% = 30 days.

Total Work (LCM of 20, 30) = 60 units. Efficiency: A = 3, B = 2.

Work by (A+B) in 9 days = (3 + 2) × 9 = 45 units. Remaining = 15 units.

Efficiency of C = 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5. Combined Eff (B+C) = 2 + 2.5 = 4.5.

Required Time (75% of 60) = (60 × 0.75) ÷ 4.5 = 45 ÷ 4.5 = 10 days.

∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

A does 20% work in 4 days ⇒ 100% work in (4 × 100/20) = 20 days.

B does 33.33% work in 10 days ⇒ 100% work in (10 × 3) = 30 days.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 20 60 (LCM) 3
B 30 2

⇒ Work done by A and B together in 9 days = (3 + 2) × 9 = 45 units.

⇒ Remaining work = Total Work − Work done = 60 − 45 = 15 units.

⇒ Remaining work completed by C in 6 days ⇒ Efficiency of C = 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5 units/day.

⇒ Target work = 75% of Total Work = 60 × 0.75 = 45 units.

⇒ Efficiency of B and C together = 2 + 2.5 = 4.5 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by B and C = 45 ÷ 4.5 = 10 days.

∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Additional Information

Work and Efficiency Relation

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. If work is constant, Efficiency ∝ 1/Time.

Combined Efficiency

Total efficiency of multiple people working together is the sum of their individual efficiencies (Etotal = E1 + E2 + ...).

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

33.33% is equivalent to 1/3, and 20% is equivalent to 1/5. Using fractions simplifies calculations in time and work problems.

questions.question: Shashi sells two articles for Rs. 5,000 each with no loss and no profit in the overall transaction. If one article is sold at \(16 \frac{2}{3}\%\) loss, then the other is sold at a profit of:
questions.questionHtml: Shashi sells two articles for Rs. 5,000 each with no loss and no profit in the overall transaction. If one article is sold at \(16 \frac{2}{3}\%\) loss, then the other is sold at a profit of:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Loss of 16 2/3% = 1/6. This means CP1 = 6 units and SP1 = 5 units.

Since SP is same for both articles, SP2 = 5 units. Total SP = 5 + 5 = 10 units.

No profit no loss implies Total CP = Total SP = 10 units.

CP2 = Total CP − CP1 = 10 − 6 = 4 units.

Profit on 2nd article = SP2 − CP2 = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

Profit % = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

∴ The correct answer is 25%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Selling Price of each article (SP) = ₹5,000

Total Selling Price = 5,000 + 5,000 = ₹10,000

Overall Profit/Loss = 0% ⇒ Total Cost Price = ₹10,000

Loss on first article = 16 2/3% = 50/3 %

Calculations:

⇒ CP1 = [SP1 × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%]

⇒ CP1 = [5,000 × 100] ÷ [100 − 50/3]

⇒ CP1 = 5,00,000 ÷ (250/3) = (5,00,000 × 3) ÷ 250 = ₹6,000

⇒ Loss on 1st article = 6,000 − 5,000 = ₹1,000

⇒ To have no profit/loss overall, Profit on 2nd article must be ₹1,000.

⇒ CP2 = SP2 − Profit = 5,000 − 1,000 = ₹4,000

⇒ Profit % on 2nd article = (1,000 ÷ 4,000) × 100 = 25%

∴ The correct answer is 25%.

Additional Information

Overall No Profit No Loss

In transactions involving two articles where SP is same and there is no overall profit or loss, the numerical value of loss on one article must equal the numerical value of profit on the other.

Successive Discounts

Equivalent single discount for two successive discounts a% and b% is given by the formula: [a + b − (a × b)/100]%.

Profit/Loss Percentage Base

Profit or Loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specified otherwise. Formula: Profit% = (Profit/CP) × 100.

questions.questionHtml: \(\frac{{sin\theta [\left( {1 - tan\theta } \right)tan\theta + {{\sec }^2}\theta ]}}{{\left( {1 - \sin \theta } \right)\tan \theta \left( {1 + tan\theta } \right)\left( {sec\theta + tan\theta } \right)}}\) is equal to:

\(\frac{{sinθ [\left( {1 - tanθ } \right)tanθ + {{\sec }^2}θ ]}}{{\left( {1 - \sin θ } \right)\tan θ \left( {1 + tanθ } \right)\left( {secθ + tanθ } \right)}}\)

\( ⇒ \;\frac{{\sin θ \;[\tan θ - \;{{\tan }^2}θ + \;1 + \;{{\tan }^2}θ ]}}{{(1 - \;\sin θ )\;\tan θ \;(1 + \;\tan θ )\;(\sec θ + \;\tan θ )}}\)

\( ⇒ \frac{{\sin θ \;(1 + \;\tan θ )}}{{(1 - \sin θ )\;\tan θ \;(1 + \;\tan θ )\;(\sec θ + \;\tan θ )}}\)

\(⇒ \;\frac{{\sin θ }}{{(1 - \;\sin θ )\;\frac{{\sin θ }}{{\cos θ }}\;(\sec θ + \;\tan θ )}}\)

\(⇒ \;\frac{{\cos θ }}{{(1 - \;\sin θ )\;\left( {\frac{1}{{\cos θ }} + \;\frac{{\sin θ }}{{\cos θ }}} \right)}}\)

questions.question: In a circle with center O, a diameter AB is produced to a point P lying outside the circle and PT is a tangent to the circle at the point C on it. If ∠BPT = 36°, then what is the measure of ∠BCP?
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with center O, a diameter AB is produced to a point P lying outside the circle and PT is a tangent to the circle at the point C on it. If ∠BPT = 36°, then what is the measure of ∠BCP?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

OC ⊥ PT (tangent ⊥ radius) ⇒ in ▵OCP, ∠COP = 90° − 36° = 54°

OB = OC (radii) ⇒ ▵OBC isosceles ⇒ ∠OCB = (180° − 54°)/2 = 63°

ABP is a straight line ⇒ ∠CBP = 180° − 63° = 117°

In ▵BCP: ∠BCP = 180° − 117° − 36° = 27°

∴ The correct answer is 27°.

Alternate Method

Given:

AB is the diameter of the circle whose centre is at O.

AB has been extended to P.

PT is the tangent at C.

∠BPT = 36°

Concept used:

The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

The sum of all angles of a triangle is 180°.

Calculation:

OC ⊥ PT at C

So, ΔOCP is a right-angled triangle at C.

Then, ∠COP = 90° - 36° = 54°

Here, OA = OB = OC = Radii of the circle.

So, ΔOBC is an isosceles triangle.

Then, ∠BCO = ∠CBO = (180° - 54°) ÷ 2 = 63°

Here, ABP is a straight line.

So, ∠CBP = 180° - 63° = 117°

Here, ΔBCP is a triangle.

So,

∠BCP + ∠CBP + ∠BPC = 180°

⇒ ∠BCP = 180° - 117° - 36°

⇒ ∠BCP = 27°

∴ The measure of ∠BCP is 27°.

Additional Information

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a chord and a tangent through one of the end points of the chord is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of the circle is always 90°.

Tangent-Radius Property

A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact (i.e., angle = 90°).

questions.question: Surekha borrowed a sum of money and returned it in two equal annual installments of Rs. 5,547 each. If the rate of interest was \(7 \frac{1}{2}\%\) p.pa compounded yearly, then the total interest paid by her was:
questions.questionHtml: Surekha borrowed a sum of money and returned it in two equal annual installments of Rs. 5,547 each. If the rate of interest was \(7 \frac{1}{2}\%\) p.pa compounded yearly, then the total interest paid by her was:
questions.solution:
FORMULA USED:

P = [(Installment)/(1 + R/100)1 + (Installment)/(1+R/100)2]

CALCULATION:

P = [(Installment)/(1 + R/100)1 + (Installment)/(1+R/100)2]

⇒ P = [5547/(43/40)1 + 5547/(43/40)2]

⇒ P = 5547(40/43 + 1600/1849)

⇒ P = 5547(3320/1849)

⇒ P = Rs. 9960

⇒ Total Installment = 5547 × 2 = Rs. 11094

⇒ Total Interest = Rs(11094 - 9960)

⇒ Rs. 1134

∴ Total interest is  Rs. 1134

questions.question: The graphs of the equations 3x - 20y - 2 = 0 and 11x - 5y + 61 = 0 intersect at P(a, b). What is the value of (a 2 + b 2 - ab)/(a 2 - b 2 + ab)?
questions.questionHtml: The graphs of the equations 3x - 20y - 2 = 0 and 11x - 5y + 61 = 0 intersect at P(a, b). What is the value of (a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> - ab)/(a<sup>2</sup> - b<sup>2</sup> + ab)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Multiply the second equation by 4 to equate the y-coefficients: 44x − 20y = −244.

Subtract the first equation (3x − 20y = 2) from this: 41x = −246 ⇒ x = −6.

Substitute x = −6 in the first equation: 3(−6) − 20y = 2 ⇒ −20y = 20 ⇒ y = −1.

Therefore, a = −6 and b = −1.

Required value = ((−6)2 + (−1)2 − (−6)(−1)) / ((−6)2 − (−1)2 + (−6)(−1)) = (36 + 1 − 6) / (36 − 1 + 6) = 31/41.

∴ The correct answer is 31/41.

Alternate Method

Given Equations: 3x − 20y = 2 and 11x − 5y = −61

⇒ Equation 1: 3x − 20y = 2

⇒ Equation 2: 11x − 5y = −61

⇒ Multiply Eq (2) by 4: 44x − 20y = −244 ... (3)

⇒ Subtracting (1) from (3): (44x − 3x) = −244 − 2

⇒ 41x = −246 ⇒ x = −6

⇒ Substitute x = −6 in (1): 3(−6) − 20y = 2

⇒ −18 − 20y = 2 ⇒ −20y = 20 ⇒ y = −1

⇒ Intersection point P(a, b) = (−6, −1) ⇒ a = −6, b = −1

⇒ Value = (a2 + b2 − ab) / (a2 − b2 + ab)

⇒ Value = [(−6)2 + (−1)2 − (−6)(−1)] / [(−6)2 − (−1)2 + (−6)(−1)]

⇒ Value = (36 + 1 − 6) / (36 − 1 + 6) = 31/41.

∴ The correct answer is 31/41.

Additional Information

Intersection of Linear Equations

Two lines a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0 intersect at a unique point if a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2.

Cramer's Rule

The solution (x, y) can be found using x = (b1c2 − b2c1)/(a1b2 − a2b1) and y = (c1a2 − c2a1)/(a1b2 − a2b1).

Algebraic Identities

The expression involves standard squares: (x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy and (x − y)2 = x2 + y2 − 2xy.

questions.question: If (10a 3 + 4b 3 ) : (11a 3 - 15b 3 ) = 7 : 5, then (3a + 5b) : (9a - 2b) =?
questions.questionHtml: If (10a<sup>3</sup> + 4b<sup>3</sup>) : (11a<sup>3</sup> - 15b<sup>3</sup>) = 7 : 5, then (3a + 5b) : (9a - 2b) =?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Cross-multiply: 5(10a3 + 4b3) = 7(11a3 − 15b3)

50a3 + 20b3 = 77a3 − 105b3 ⇒ 27a3 = 125b3

Taking cube root: a/b = 5/3

Substitute a = 5, b = 3 in (3a + 5b) : (9a − 2b)

(15 + 15) : (45 − 6) = 30 : 39 = 10 : 13

∴ The correct answer is 10 : 13.

Alternate Method

Given:

(10a3 + 4b3) : (11a3 − 15b3) = 7 : 5

Formula Used:

If a : b = c : d, then ad = bc.

Calculations:

⇒ (10a3 + 4b3) / (11a3 − 15b3) = 7 / 5

⇒ 5 × (10a3 + 4b3) = 7 × (11a3 − 15b3)

⇒ 50a3 + 20b3 = 77a3 − 105b3

⇒ 20b3 + 105b3 = 77a3 − 50a3

⇒ 125b3 = 27a3

⇒ a3/b3 = 125/27

⇒ a/b = 3√(125/27) = 5/3

⇒ Now, substitute a = 5k and b = 3k in the required expression:

⇒ [3(5k) + 5(3k)] : [9(5k) − 2(3k)]

⇒ (15k + 15k) : (45k − 6k)

⇒ 30k : 39k

⇒ 30 : 39 = 10 : 13

∴ The correct answer is 10 : 13.

Additional Information

Triplicate Ratio

The triplicate ratio of a : b is defined as a3 : b3. Conversely, the sub-triplicate ratio is the cube root ratio.

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If a/b = c/d, then (a + b)/(a − b) = (c + d)/(c − d). This is often used to solve ratio equations involving higher powers.

Ratio as Fraction

A ratio a : b can always be treated as a fraction a/b for algebraic manipulation, maintaining the equality across cross-multiplication.

questions.question: In ΔABC, ∠A - ∠B = 33°, ∠B - ∠C = 18° What is the sum of the smallest and the largest angles of the triangle?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, ∠A - ∠B = 33°, ∠B - ∠C = 18° What is the sum of the smallest and the largest angles of the triangle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let ∠B = x.

Given ∠A − ∠B = 33° and ∠B − ∠C = 18°.

⇒ ∠A = x + 33° and ∠C = x − 18°.

Sum of angles: (x + 33°) + x + (x − 18°) = 180° ⇒ 3x + 15° = 180° ⇒ x = 55°.

Largest ∠A = 55° + 33° = 88° and Smallest ∠C = 55° − 18° = 37°.

Sum of Smallest and Largest = 88° + 37° = 125°.

∴ The correct answer is 125°.

Alternate Method

Given:

∠A − ∠B = 33°

∠B − ∠C = 18°

Formula:

In any triangle ABC, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

Step-by-step Calculation:

⇒ ∠A = ∠B + 33°

⇒ ∠C = ∠B − 18°

Substituting values in the angle sum formula:

⇒ (∠B + 33°) + ∠B + (∠B − 18°) = 180°

⇒ 3 × ∠B + 15° = 180°

⇒ 3 × ∠B = 180° − 15°

⇒ 3 × ∠B = 165°

⇒ ∠B = 165° ÷ 3 = 55°

Finding all individual angles:

⇒ ∠A = 55° + 33° = 88° (Largest angle)

⇒ ∠C = 55° − 18° = 37° (Smallest angle)

Calculation of the required sum:

⇒ Sum = ∠A + ∠C = 88° + 37° = 125°

∴ The correct answer is 125°.

Additional Information

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles in any Euclidean triangle is always 180°.

Angle-Side Relationship

In a triangle, the side opposite the largest angle is the longest side, and the side opposite the smallest angle is the shortest side.

Exterior Angle Theorem

An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles (e.g., Exterior ∠A = ∠B + ∠C).

Classification by Angles

Triangles are classified as Acute (all angles < 90°), Right (one angle = 90°), or Obtuse (one angle > 90°).

questions.question: Three men and 4 women can do a piece of work in 7 days, whereas 2 men and 1 woman can do it in 14 days. Seven women will complete the same work in:
questions.questionHtml: Three men and 4 women can do a piece of work in 7 days, whereas 2 men and 1 woman can do it in 14 days. Seven women will complete the same work in:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Equate total work: (3M + 4W) × 7 = (2M + 1W) × 14

⇒ 3M + 4W = 2(2M + 1W) ⇒ 3M + 4W = 4M + 2W ⇒ 1M = 2W

Total work in terms of women = (3 × 2W + 4W) × 7 = 70W

Number of days for 7 women = 70W ÷ 7W = 10 days

∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Alternate Method

Given: (3M + 4W) complete work in 7 days; (2M + 1W) complete work in 14 days.

Formula Used: Total Work = Efficiency × Time; Efficiency × Time = Constant

Group Days Total Work (LCM) Efficiency
3M + 4W 7 14 units 2
2M + 1W 14 1

⇒ Efficiency of 3M + 4W = 2 −−− (i)

⇒ Efficiency of 2M + 1W = 1 −−− (ii)

⇒ From (i) and (ii): 3M + 4W = 2(2M + 1W)

⇒ 3M + 4W = 4M + 2W ⇒ 1M = 2W

⇒ Substitute M = 2W in (ii): 2(2W) + 1W = 1 ⇒ 5W = 1 ⇒ W = 1/5 unit/day

⇒ Efficiency of 7 women = 7 × W = 7 × (1/5) = 7/5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by 7 women = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 14 ÷ (7/5)

⇒ Time = 14 × (5/7) = 10 days

∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Additional Information

M-D-H Relation

For group work, use (M1×D1×H1)/W1 = (M2×D2×H2)/W2 to compare different sets of workers and work done.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the same amount of work. If Time ratio is x:y, Efficiency ratio is y:x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by individuals, which is (Efficiency × Time).
